generateStyleSVG

Style code and local writing

On this page

generateStyleSVG ​

Generate a compact, square, QR-inspired SVG code from seven writing-style signals.

Syntax ​

javascript
const svg = WriteLikeMe.generateStyleSVG(categories, width, height);

Parameters ​

ParameterTypeDefaultDescription
categoriesobject{}Category weights from 0 to 1; omitted categories default to 0.5
widthnumber320SVG canvas width in pixels
heightnumber320SVG canvas height in pixels

Supported category keys are formality, complexity, sentence_length, vocabulary, tone, creativity, and punctuation. A score of 0 is valid.

Returns ​

A string containing a dark, square SVG. Its seven horizontal bands correspond to formality (F), complexity (C), sentence length (L), vocabulary (V), tone (T), creativity (R), and punctuation balance (P). The first six bands contain 54 circular cells each; score controls how many are emphasized and their radius. The punctuation band uses 54 comma marks and period dots, with the comma share controlled by the punctuation score. The design is QR-inspired but is not a scannable QR code. The “WriteLikeMe Code” label appears at the bottom left. The SVG also contains a versioned JSON profile in a <metadata> element. When the input is an analyzeText result, this metadata includes its voice cues and frequent words as well as the seven visible category scores. Review the metadata before sharing: frequent words may reveal information about the source text.

Use readStyleCode(svg) to retrieve the profile. SVGs created before metadata was added are read as an approximate seven-category profile.

Example ​

javascript
const WriteLikeMe = require('@ai-clyde/writelikeme');
const fs = require('fs');

const profile = WriteLikeMe.analyzeText('A sample sentence.');
const svg = WriteLikeMe.generateStyleSVG(profile);
fs.writeFileSync('writelikeme-code.svg', svg);

Category scores are expected to be numeric values from 0 through 1.
